chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him): When Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah have mercy on him) was sent to Az-Zubayr before the outbreak of the war on the Day of the Camel, to advise him back to obedience,
he said to him on that occasion:

key_terms.الزُّبَيْر: Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, a prominent companion and general
key_terms.طَاعَتِهِ: His obedience (referring to Imam Ali's authority)
key_terms.لِيَسْتَفِيئَهُ: To advise him or call him back (to obedience)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُل: The Day of the Camel, referring to the Battle of Basra

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam Ali send to advise Az-Zubayr before the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: This narration highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) strategic preference for diplomacy and unity over immediate conflict, sending the learned Abdullah ibn Abbas to persuade Az-Zubayr to join the Caliphate before the Battle of the Camel. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that Ali’s actions were driven by a desire to establish legitimate authority and resolve disputes through counsel, reflecting the Quranic principle of reconciliation among believers.
